conventions.convention: Physical-time dynamics uses α_t(X)=exp(itH/ℏ)X exp(−itH/ℏ). For β>0 in J⁻¹ and ℏ>0 in J s, the closed KMS strip has width b=βℏ seconds. Its lower boundary is ω(Aα_t(B)); its upper boundary is ω(α_t(B)A).
KMS correlation functions are bounded on the entire closed strip, continuous there, and holomorphic in its interior. Invariance is derived, rather than included in the KMS definition.

Three-lines interpolation is asserted only for 0<s<b; both exponents are positive, and 0^r=0 for r>0. Equality on the lower edge determines a bounded continuous holomorphic strip function, including its upper edge.

Finite-volume Gibbs states use free-boundary Hamiltonians along increasing finite exhaustions indexed by n≥1. Their extensions adjoin the normalized trace density q⁻¹I at each outside site. Limits are pointwise limits of functionals on the quasi-local algebra.

Infinite-spin existence retains Countable Choice, finite on-site dimension, uniformly bounded finite-range interactions, and the exact finite-matrix C*-identity and state/density-norm interfaces. It asserts neither uniqueness nor a global trace-class Gibbs density nor physical relaxation.
Finite Gibbs characterization applies to a nonzero finite-dimensional Hilbert space and β>0; dimension one and degenerate Hamiltonian eigenvalues are included.

load_bearing.statement: A state is β-KMS when every observable pair admits a bounded continuous function on 0≤Im z≤βℏ, holomorphic inside, with lower boundary ω(Aα_t(B)) and upper boundary ω(α_t(B)A).

For a bounded continuous F on S_b, holomorphic inside, the interior horizontal supremum is at most M₀^(1−s/b)M₁^(s/b), 0<s<b. Boundary bounds therefore control the whole strip, and identical lower boundary values imply equality throughout the closed strip.

Under the stated finite-spin, finite-range, Countable Choice and finite-matrix interfaces, the specified finite Gibbs extensions have a pointwise-convergent subsequence. Every pointwise-convergent subsequence and its state limit admit bounded continuous analytic strip functions with the required KMS boundaries for every fixed strictly local observable pair.

For nonzero finite-dimensional H, a self-adjoint Hamiltonian, β>0 and ℏ>0, under the stated finite spectral-calculus and C*-algebra clauses, a state is β-KMS for exp(itH/ℏ)(·)exp(−itH/ℏ) if and only if it is the normalized Gibbs trace state.

Under its explicit hypotheses, every pointwise-convergent subsequence of the specified free-boundary finite Gibbs extensions has a full-algebra β-KMS limit for the thermodynamic dynamics, and at least one such subsequential limit exists.

seams_checked.note: The definition and existence arguments retain Countable Choice, finite-matrix interfaces, finite-range bounds and free-boundary exhaustion conventions. They use compact-time norm convergence and the local generator at their stated scope.

The diagonal-reduction lemma and KMS–DLR theorem preserve bounded closed-strip regularity, lower-edge uniqueness, βℏ width, reversed upper-edge ordering and the finite Gibbs characterization's hypotheses. They supply their own local-to-full-algebra extension.

The onsite product theorem uses the Gibbs-strip supplier only for local pairs, proves the all-observable extension separately, and applies finite Gibbs uniqueness only after establishing invariance of each finite local algebra under onsite dynamics.

The orbit clock theorem preserves the full KMS definition in both directions: α^λ_τ=α_(τ/λ) gives inverse temperature λβ, and the converse gives β̂/λ. Positive constant λ rescales the closed strip and both boundaries; the geometric interpretation applies separately along constant-lapse orbits.
